Scientific name: Clarias angolensis Steindachner, 1866

Common name: Angolan Walking Catfish

Type locality: Angola.

Size: 35 cm SL (13.8")

Etymology: Clarias: from the Greek chlaros, meaning lively, in reference to the ability of the fish to live for long periods out of water. Named after Angola, its country of discovery.
Africa: Lower and Central Congo system. Trade restricted in Germany (Anl.3 BArtSchV).

• pH: 6.8 - 8.5
  • Temperature: 22.0-25.0°C
  • Able to survive in most water conditions.
Open spaces for swimming and some cover is required.
Omnivorous and predatory. Will eat virtually anything that can be considered edible.
Must be housed with lively, robust large fish. Suggested tankmates: large cyprinids (silver sharks, tinfoil or spanner barbs for example) or Central American cichlids.
Males are brighter and more slender than females.

Sexually mature at 2.5 years. Spawning in pairs. Lithophilous species. Fecundity over 500 cream-coloured eggs (diameter of around 2 mm). The male protects the clutch. Incubation period 1.5 to 2 days, after 4-5 days the young start feeding. There is no breeding report.

Clarias species are characterized by an elongated body; a soft rayed dorsal fin extending to, or nearly to, the caudal fin base; a soft rayed anal fin extending from just behind the anus to the caudal fin base; pectoral fins each with a serrated anterior bony spine; head depressed, covered largely by firmly sutured, surface sculptured bony plates forming a protective helmet; four pairs of flagellate barbels (nasals, maxillaries, inner and outer mandibulars); air breathing organs derived from the 2nd and 4th epibranchials within a superbranchial chamber.

Coloration is brownish, albino varieties are also known.
Verhandlungen der K.-K. zoologisch-botanischen Gesellschaft in Wien v. 16, pp 766, Pl. 13 (figs. 4-7).
